areas.populationBasis: Geographic whole-block internal-point assignment; not wastewater customers or dependent/affected people.

populationMethod: Select distinct exact source BASINID labels of the relevant public station records. Assign a 2020 Census block to a basin when its official internal point lies inside or on the published basin polygon (multipart features are unioned). Union block GEOIDs across every selected basin and count each block population once. This is a dated geographic population-context estimate, not a customer/dependency/outage or flood-exposed population estimate.

utilitySummary.label: St. Petersburg three-facility reported annual treatment throughput

limitations: The public station basin label and City polygon BASINID establish an identifier association, not verified wastewater service dependence, customer count, hydraulic connectivity or an outage footprint.

A resident is counted geographically by the internal point of the whole Census block; a basin crossing a block may include residents on its other side or omit residents on this side. This is not an address-level or exact partial-block population allocation.
Population and housing are 2020 Census counts, not current occupancy, visitors, customers, connections, flood-exposed people, people without service or an illness/casualty estimate.
Overlapping basins or multiple selected stations sharing a basin must be deduplicated by block GEOID, never by summing station or area population totals.
Source boundaries and station points can differ at edges; the exact source label is used, not a nearest-polygon assignment. Multipart source features share one basin identifier and are unioned.
Only source basins referenced by the station register are packaged; these do not establish the complete City wastewater service territory or a municipal population denominator.

No measured sub-basin population, sewer connection count or flow is published in the City sub-basin schema. Separately sourced flow aggregates cannot be silently assigned to these geographic footprints.
WWTF flow is actual wastewater through the treatment facility on an average annual basis; it is not current telemetry, distributed reuse water or spill volume.
The reporting period follows FDEP's annual reuse year, October 1 through September 30; this convention is explicitly documented in the 2025 Reuse Inventory Report.
Permitted capacity is a regulatory treatment maximum, not measured available capacity, redundancy or guaranteed storm performance.
Whole-facility throughput is not apportioned to screened stations, Census blocks or sewer sub-basins without a verified service/flow crosswalk.
Equivalent historical throughput in gallons equals annual average MGD times 1,000,000 times window hours divided by 24; this arithmetic is not forecast wastewater spill or service loss.
No per-person wastewater rate, repair factor, damage amount, outage duration or FEMA funding offset is inferred from these records.
